sentences.en: Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 你好,这是6分钟英语 从英国广播公司学习英语。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. In English, there are many ways to describe smells.
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔,我是乔治,英语里有多种描述气味的方法

sentences.en: Poet Michael Rosen wanted to find words describing bad smells, and asked listeners of his BBC Radio 4 programme Word of Mouth for some suggestions.
sentences.zh: 诗人迈克尔·罗森想找到描述臭味的词,并问BBC电台4号节目的听众要一些建议。

sentences.en: Fusty, reeking, toiking, honking, humming, funky… Smells are everywhere, whether they're bad smells like rotten eggs and sweaty feet, or pleasant ones like lavender and freshly baked bread.
sentences.zh: 发臭,发臭,发臭,吹喇叭,哼哼,发臭...

sentences.en: What smells do you especially like or dislike, Georgie?
sentences.zh: 你特别喜欢或不喜欢什么味道,乔治?

sentences.en: Well, I really enjoy the smell of leather, but something I really love is the smell of rain, which has a name.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我真的很喜欢皮革的味道, 但我真的喜欢的是雨的味道, 它有一个名字。

sentences.en: Do you know it, Neil? Erm, I don't think I do actually.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗,尼尔?

sentences.en: It's called petrichor. It's that smell of the ground just after it's rained.
sentences.zh: 这叫石器 雨刚下完就闻到了地面的气味

sentences.en: Mmm. Neil, what about you? Which smells do you like?
sentences.zh: 尼尔 你呢 你喜欢哪个味道

sentences.en: Well, I don't think you can beat the smell of a freshly opened packet of ground coffee.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我不认为你能战胜气味 新鲜打开的一包 地面咖啡。

sentences.en: Ooh, that's a good one. In this episode, we'll be learning the language of smells using some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 哦,这是一个很好的一集。在这个集中,我们将学习 气味的语言 使用一些有用的新词和短语。

sentences.en: And remember, you can find all the vocabulary plus a quiz and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 并记住,你可以找到所有的词汇 加上一个测验和工作表 在我们的网站,bbc学习英语. com。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 但首先 我有个问题要问你 乔治

sentences.en: One smell many people love is the smell of old books and the sentimental feeling it gives them for second-hand bookshops.
sentences.zh: 许多人喜欢的味道是旧书的味道 和他们对于二手书店的感情

sentences.en: In fact, there's even a word for it, but what is it?
sentences.zh: 事实上,它甚至有一个词, 但是它是什么?

sentences.en: Is it: a) vellichor, b) petrichor, or c) nidor?
sentences.zh: 是:a) Vellichor,b) 石墨,或c) 尼多尔?

sentences.en: Well, we already know that petrichor is the smell of the ground after rain.
sentences.zh: 嗯,我们已经知道, 彼得里奇是地面的气味 雨后。

sentences.en: I'm going to go with a) vellichor. Well, we'll find out at the end of the programme.
sentences.zh: 我会和Vellichor一起去的 我们会在节目结束时知道的

sentences.en: Listening to Michael Rosen's list – funky, reeking, humming and the rest – you might think English is good at describing smells, but in fact, all those words really mean is bad smelling.
sentences.zh: 听迈克尔·罗森的名单 — — 发臭、发臭、哼哼等等 — — 你可能会认为英语在描述气味方面是好的,但事实上,所有这些词其实都意味着臭味。

sentences.en: In English, we often describe smells by comparing them to other objects.
sentences.zh: 在英语中,我们常常用与其他物体相比来描述气味。

sentences.en: For example, something nice might smell like a rose, while something bad might smell like rotten eggs, but there are few words to describe the actual smell itself.
sentences.zh: 例如,一些好东西可能闻起来像玫瑰, 而一些坏东西可能闻起来像腐烂的鸡蛋, 但有几句话来描述实际的气味本身。

sentences.en: Oxford University psychologist Asifa Majid has researched the subject of smell extensively.
sentences.zh: 牛津大学心理学家Asifa Majid广泛研究了嗅觉问题。

sentences.en: Here, she tells Michael Rosen a little of what she's found out on BBC Radio 4 programme Word of Mouth.
sentences.zh: 在这里,她告诉迈克尔・罗森 在BBC电台的4个节目《嘴的文字》 发现了一些她发现的东西。

sentences.en: So, if we think about things like stinky or fragrant, they're definitely telling us that something is good or bad.
sentences.zh: 所以,如果我们想到 臭或香的东西, 他们肯定告诉我们 东西是好的或坏的。

sentences.en: But unlike colour terms, it doesn't really seem to be about the object it's describing.
sentences.zh: 但与颜色术语不同, 它似乎并不真正 与它描述的对象。

sentences.en: It seems to be a subjective thing. I could say, "Oh this perfume you think is really fragrant, I think is stinky," and both can be true.
sentences.zh: 这似乎是主观的。我可以说,“哦,你认为这个香水非常香,我觉得很臭。” 两者都是真实的。

sentences.en: Describing smell is not like describing other senses.
sentences.zh: 描述气味和描述其他感官不一样

sentences.en: I might think a perfume is stinky, an adjective meaning bad smelling, while Neil might find the same perfume fragrant, meaning pleasant smelling.
sentences.zh: 我可能觉得香水很臭, 形容词的意思是臭味, 而尼尔可能会发现同样的香水香味, 意思是香味。

sentences.en: Both can be true. The point is that neither stinky nor fragrant say anything specific about the perfume's actual smell.
sentences.zh: 两者都是真实的 重点是 香水和臭味 都不具体提到香水的味道

sentences.en: With our sense of taste, it's different.
sentences.zh: 我们的品味不同

sentences.en: Words like spicy, sweet or salty create a common idea that we can all agree on, but that's not the case for smells.
sentences.zh: 诸如辣、甜或咸之类的词 创造了一个我们都能同意的共同点子 但闻起来不是这样的

sentences.en: Asifa thinks this is because, unlike tastes and colours, smell words are subjective – they're based on personal opinions and feelings rather than objective truth.
sentences.zh: 阿西法认为这与品味和颜色不同,

sentences.en: This might explain why our attitude to talking about smells is so different.
sentences.zh: 这也许可以解释为什么我们对谈论气味的态度如此不同。

sentences.en: Here's Asifa again, sharing some examples of how we talk about smells with BBC Radio 4.
sentences.zh: 这是Asifa 和BBC第四电台分享一些关于我们如何谈论气味的例子。

sentences.en: So, if we compare how often people talk about visual things, or auditory things, or tastes or smells, what we find is we talk a lot about what we see and very rarely about what we smell.
sentences.zh: 所以,如果我们比较人们经常谈论视觉的东西, 或听觉的东西, 或味道或气味, 我们发现我们经常谈论我们所看到的东西, 很少谈论我们闻到的东西。

sentences.en: Young children in the UK are often interested in the sense of smell and they'll remark on it, and the parent will shut it down.
sentences.zh: 英国的幼童往往对嗅觉感兴趣, 他们会对此发表评论, 家长会关闭它。

sentences.en: They'll say, "That's disgusting! Put it down."
sentences.zh: 他们会说,"真恶心,放下"

sentences.en: Asifa's research shows that, here in the UK at least, people talk about visual or auditory things much more than they talk about smells.
sentences.zh: Asifa的研究显示,至少在英国这里, 人们谈论视觉或听觉的事情比谈论气味要多得多。

sentences.en: The adjective visual means related to seeing, and auditory means related to hearing.
sentences.zh: 与视觉有关的形容词 与听力有关的形容词

sentences.en: The adjective for things related to smelling is olfactory.
sentences.zh: 有关嗅觉的形容词是嗅觉。

sentences.en: Maybe this is because of how we're raised by our parents.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为我们的父母抚养我们长大了

sentences.en: When children start talking about smells, especially unpleasant ones, parents often react by shutting the conversation down.
sentences.zh: 当孩子开始谈论气味, 特别是不愉快的气味, 父母往往反应 关闭谈话。

sentences.en: The phrase to shut something down means to stop it.
sentences.zh: 关闭东西的短语 意味着阻止它。

sentences.en: Along with other European languages, English doesn't have much vocabulary dedicated to the different qualities of actual smells.
sentences.zh: 与其它欧洲语言一样,英语没有太多的词汇 专门用来形容不同品质的实际气味。

sentences.en: There are many ways of talking about smells, especially unpleasant ones, but only a few words which describe actual smells themselves.
sentences.zh: 有很多方式谈论气味, 特别是不愉快的气味, 但只有几句话 描述真实的气味自己。

sentences.en: A good example of a word which does this is musty – a damp, stale smell you might find in an old bookshop.
sentences.zh: 这个词的好例子就是一团乱 潮湿的臭味 可能在旧书店里找到

sentences.en: And Neil, that reminds me of your question.
sentences.zh: 尼尔,这让我想起你的问题

sentences.en: That's right. I asked you what the word is, which means the smell of old books.
sentences.zh: 没错 我问你这个词是什么 意思是旧书的味道

sentences.en: I said it was vellichor. Well, Georgie, you are absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我说了是维利科,乔治,你说得对

sentences.en: Yay! Petrichor, as you said earlier, is the smell of the earth after rain.
sentences.zh: 佩特里奇,正如你先前所说,是雨后的大地的气味

sentences.en: And nidor is the smell of cooking meat and fat.
sentences.zh: 尼多是煮肉和脂肪的味道

sentences.en: OK. It's time for a recap of the vocabulary we've learned.
sentences.zh: 好了 是时候总结一下我们学到的词汇了

sentences.en: The adjective stinky means foul smelling, while the adjective fragrant means pleasant smelling.
sentences.zh: 形容词臭味的意思是臭味,形容词香味的意思是香味。

sentences.en: Subjective things are based on your own personal opinions and feelings rather than objective facts.
sentences.zh: 主观的东西是基于你的个人观点和感情 而不是客观的事实

sentences.en: The adjective visual describes things related to seeing, while auditory means related to hearing.
sentences.zh: 形容词“视觉”描述了与视觉有关的东西,而“听觉”是指与听觉有关的东西。

sentences.en: Things related to smelling are called olfactory.
sentences.zh: 与嗅觉有关的东西叫做嗅觉。

sentences.en: And finally, the phrasal verb to shut something down means to stop it.
sentences.zh: 最后, 关闭某物的语句动词 意味着阻止它。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but there's still time to head over to our website, bbclearningenglish.com, for a quiz and worksheet containing all the vocabulary we've discussed.
sentences.zh: 再一次,我们的六分钟到了, 但是还有时间去我们的网站,bbc 学习英语.com, 一个包含我们讨论过的词汇的测验和工作单。

sentences.en: See you again soon! But for now, it's goodbye.
sentences.zh: 很快再见,但现在再见了

sentences.en: Goodbye!
sentences.zh: 再见!
